c-sd-basic.label: Speed, distance and time: units first
c-sd-basic.summary: One formula and one habit: write minutes and hours in the same unit before dividing.

c-sd-relative.label: Relative speed: meeting and chasing
c-sd-relative.summary: Towards each other speeds add; in the same direction they subtract.

c-sd-circular.label: Overtaking on a track
c-sd-circular.summary: The faster one overtakes after closing the gap between them at the relative speed.

q-sd-convert.label: Same distance, different time or route
q-sd-convert.summary: Distance changes by a percentage, time is fixed, find the new speed.

q-sd-units.label: A rate in short time scaled to a long time
q-sd-units.summary: Distance in 1 minute; find the distance in hours.

q-sd-meet.label: Two bodies meet: opposite or same direction
q-sd-meet.summary: Two meeting times give two equations: sum and difference of speeds.

q-sd-overtake.label: First overtake on a circular track
q-sd-overtake.summary: Gap ÷ relative speed gives the time; times the faster speed gives the distance.

formulas.note: Put minutes and hours in one unit first.

formulas.text: Same time: speed ∝ distance     Same distance: speed ∝ 1 ÷ time
formulas.note: 25% more distance in the same time needs 25% more speed.

formulas.text: Opposite: relative speed = u + v     Same direction: = u − v
First overtake: time = gap ÷ (u − v); distance by the faster = u × time
formulas.note: The track length matters only if the gap is more than one lap.

q-sd-convert.cue: 'Distance increases by 25%… must still arrive in the same time. New speed?'
q-sd-convert.standard: Same time, so speed grows with distance: 200 × 1.25 = 250 km/h.
q-sd-convert.fast: The 40 minutes cancels. Raise the speed by the same 25%: 200 + 50.
q-sd-convert.eliminate: More distance in the same time means a higher speed, so the answer is above 200, and 25% of 200 is exactly 50.
traps: Taking 25% of the time instead of the distance.
Working out time from the 40 minutes and not cancelling it.

q-sd-units.cue: 'A train covers 1.2 km in 1 minute. How far in 2 h 15 min?'
q-sd-units.eliminate: 1.2 km a minute is 72 km/h. In 2.25 hours that is between 72 × 2 = 144 and 72 × 2.5 = 180, and 72 × 2.25 is exactly 162.
traps: Treating 1.2 km as 1.2 km/h without the minute.

q-sd-meet.cue: Two bodies start a fixed distance apart; one meeting time towards each other and another in the same direction.
q-sd-meet.standard: Towards: u + v = 480 ÷ 5 = 96. Same direction: u − v = 480 ÷ 15 = 32. So u = (96 + 32) ÷ 2 = 64.
q-sd-meet.fast: The faster speed is the average of the sum and the difference: (96 + 32)/2.
q-sd-meet.eliminate: The faster speed must exceed half the sum (48) and be less than the sum (96). Test each option: v = 96 − u must be below u and u − v must equal 32.
traps: Using 480 ÷ 15 as one of the speeds.
Choosing the slower speed, 32, as the answer.

q-sd-overtake.cue: A circular track, two starts with the second ahead by some distance, and 'when does he overtake for the first time'.
q-sd-overtake.standard: Relative speed 20 − 8 = 12 m/s. Gap 500 m, so time = 500 ÷ 12. Distance of the motorcycle = 20 × 500/12 = 833.33 m.
q-sd-overtake.eliminate: The motorcycle covers more than the 500 m gap (it must close it at 12 of its 20 m/s), so it travels about 500 × 20/12 ≈ 833 m. 800 m is too short and 1,800 m is far too long.
traps: Giving the truck's distance (333.33 m) rather than the motorcycle's.
Adding the speeds, as if they met head on.
Using the track length of 2.2 km, which is irrelevant here.

solution: Time is fixed, so speed is proportional to distance.

pyqs.text: Two motorcycles M and N start from points 480 km apart. Moving towards each other they meet in 5 hours; moving in the same direction they meet in 15 hours. What is the speed of M, the faster motorcycle?
solution: Towards each other: M + N = 480 ÷ 5 = 96 km/h.
